[Bhuvan Shome (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064086/?ref_=ls_knf_24)

Sen is one of his nation's most politically active filmakers. After having studied physics at university in Calcutta, Sen worked as a freelance journalist, a salesman of patent medicines and a sound technician in a film studio. In the mid-1940s he joined the Indian People's Theatre Association and at that time began to read about and study film. The association had links to the Communist Party of India and this heralded the beginning of Sen's involvement with Marxist politics. In 1956 Sen made his debut with [Raat Bhore (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049649/?ls), the first of his 30 (as of 2002) films. Although his first film was openly political, he achieved national status as the director of a comedy, [Bhuvan Shome (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064086/?ls). Influenced by Italian neorealism and the work of fellow countryman [Satyajit Ray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006249/?ls), Sen used location shooting and non-professional casts in his early films. By the 1970s he was making wider use of symbolism and allegory. Although he remains politically committed, Sen feels that the "difference between party Marxists and a private Marxist like me is that others think they pocketed truth, whereas I am always in search of truth... " Sen's films have won numerous international awards. [The Case Is Closed (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084198/?ls), a scathing look at the hypocritical reaction of a bourgeois Calcutta family to the death of a servant boy, took home the Jury Prize from the 1983 Cannes Film Festival.

# The Best Film Directors of Indian Cinema

These are the directors born in India, who have made such great movies that their name will live for centuries even when they won't be there.  
Some of these are already legends, like Satyajit Ray, Hrishikesh and Shyam Benegal.  
Some of these are legends in making and have proved their mettle time again and again like Sanjay Leela Bhansali, Ram Gopal Varma and Maniratnam.  
Some have simply re-defined the Indian Cinema like Vishal Bhardwaj, Anurag Kashyap and Dibakar Banerjee.  
And some of these, though, have only two or three movies to their names like Shojit Sircar and Vikramaditya Motwane, but those two or three movies have assured that these directors will have a great impact on Indian Cinema in future.  
  
The list doesn't boast of any Indian who has garnered fame in Hollywood like Tarsem Singh, M Night Shayamalan, Shakhar Kapur, Mira Nair, Deepa Mehta OR Gurinder Chaddha etc...  
  
PS: I have included only those directors in the list of who's work I have seen. NOM to any fan of some person who is not included in the list.  
PPS: I haven't rated them better or best, all of them are great, so please ignore the sequence.

 #### [1. Satyajit Ray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006249/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Writer
    *   Composer
    *   Director

[Pather Panchali (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048473/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

[Satyajit Ray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006249/?ls) was born in Calcutta on May 2, 1921. His father, Late [Sukumar Ray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm7861218/?ls) was an eminent poet and writer in the history of Bengali literature. In 1940, after receiving his degree in science and economics from Calcutta University, he attended Tagore's Viswa-Bharati University. His first movie [Pather Panchali (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048473/?ls) won several International Awards and set Ray as a world-class director. He died on April twenty-third, 1992.

 #### [2. Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0611531/?ref_=ls_t_2) 

    *   Director
    *   Editor
    *   Writer

[Anand (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066763/?ref_=ls_knf_2)

By no means is he any glamorous director, yet Hrishikesh Mukherjee is one of the most popular and beloved filmmakers in Indian cinema. His magic lay not in the glamor or largeness so often associated with cinema, but in its simplicity and warmth.  
  
He began his career in Bombay, 1951, as an editor and assistant director to Bimal Roy, another great director himself. His first directorial venture, [Musafir (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050734/?ls), centering on an old house where three unrelated stories dealing with birth, marriage and death occur in a series, was a disaster. But director Raj Kapoor was impressed and strongly recommended Hrishida as director for [Anari (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052560/?ls). Starring Kapoor himself and Nutan, the film was a critical and commercial success.  
  
His next film, [Anuradha (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0137362/?ls), about an idealistic doctor who neglects his wife to focus on his work, got him the President's Medal Award. But from then on throughout the 1960s decade, none of Hrishida films were particularly distinguishable, barring Asli-Naqli (1962), a Muslim melodrama; [Anupama (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0137361/?ls), which was based on a true incident; [Aashirwad (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0147855/?ls), a family drama; and [Satyakam (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0244776/?ls), about an idealist seeing his dreams crumble after Indian independence.  
  
Then Hrishida made what is considered his masterpiece - [Anand (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066763/?ls). This classic film gave a complex but compassionate look at the balance between hope, fear, life and death and saw Rajesh Khanna's greatest performance as a terminally ill man who wishes to live life to the full before he dies. It was an auspicious beginning to the 1970s, for that time proved to be an exceptionally good time for Hrishida as he gave the public excellent films like Guddi (1971), a semi-satiric look at the film industry and generally considered as Jaya Bhaduri's debut film; [Abhimaan (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0069671/?ls), the Bachchans' greatest ever performance together; and [Chupke Chupke (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072783/?ls), a comedy about a newlywed professor's joke on his pompous brother-in-law. These films gave an extremely skilled and detailed look at the middle-class mentality.  
  
Few people understood human nature as well as Hrishida - in all his films he examined their aspects, particularly their failings and foibles and the outworn values people always seem to hold on to. However in the 1980s, the advent of the superstar Amitabh Bachchan and of larger-than-life films saw Hrishida's brand of filmmaking die out. Recently he attempted a comeback with _Jhooth Bole Kauwa Kaate (1999)_, but sadly it was a futile effort as the film was a commercial and critical failure. However, the magic of his films still lingers after three decades, and he will be best remembered for his film [Anand (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066763/?ls), which told that people who die but remain in heart and mind do not die, but become immortal. No one justifies this truth more than Hrishida.

![Image 5: Guru Dutt in Thirst (1957)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjA0Mzg2NjEwN15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwODQ1NDQzNzE@._V1_QL75_UY60_CR10,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0244870/?ref_=ls_i_3)  

 #### [3. Guru Dutt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0244870/?ref_=ls_t_3) 

    *   Actor
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[Thirst (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050870/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

Considered to be a man ahead of his time, Guru Dutt was one of the greatest icons of commercial Indian cinema. Although he made less than ten films, they are believed to be the best to come from Bollywood's Golden Age, known both for their ability to reach out to the common man and for their artistic and lyrical content, and they went on to become trend-setters that have influenced Bollywood ever since. But for all his genius, there was a shroud of tragedy that overshadowed his career and life.  
  
Dutt was born in Mysore on July ninth, 1925, the eldest son of a headmaster and a housewife who was a part-time writer. As a child, he had to deal with a strained relationship between his parents, hostility from his mother's family, and the death of a close relative. He received his early education in Calcutta, and in 1941, he joined the Uday Shankar India Culture Center, where he received basic training in the performing arts under dance maestro [Uday Shankar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1142684/?ls). Afterward, in 1944, he had a short stint as a telephone operator.  
  
Dutt entered the Indian film industry in 1944, working as a choreographer in Prabhat Studios. There, he became friends with [Dev Anand](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007147/?ls) (whom he met when they worked on the film [Hum Ek Hain (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0269343/?ls)) and [Rehman Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0716839/?ls). These early friendships helped ease his way into Bollywood. After Prabhat went under in 1947, Dutt moved to Mumbai, where he worked with the leading directors of the time: [Amiya Chakrabarty](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0149810/?ls) in [Girls' School (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0157702/?ls) and [Gyan Mukherjee](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0611527/?ls) in [Sangram (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0244181/?ls).  
  
He got his big break when [Dev Anand](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007147/?ls) invited him to direct a film in his newly formed company Navketan Films. Dutt made his directorial debut with [Gamble (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043307/?ls), which starred [Dev Anand](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007147/?ls). The film was an urban crime thriller that paid homage to classic film noir. However, it also carried its own elements that ensured it was not a remake of a Hollywood film: notably, songs were used to further the story's narrative, and close-up shots were used frequently. The film was a success and became a trend-setter for future crime films. On the personal front, Dutt met his wife, playback singer [Geeta Dutt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0244869/?ls) (née Roy), during the song-recording sessions of [Gamble (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043307/?ls), and they married May twenty-sixth, 1953.  
  
Dutt's next releases were [The Trap (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044761/?ls) and [Falcon (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045529/?ls). Dutt made his acting debut in the latter film, which he also directed. But while they were average successes, he finally tasted success with [This or That (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046673/?ls), another crime thriller, but with a far more polished story and look. Then came [Mr. & Mrs. '55 (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048392/?ls), a frothy romantic comedy focusing on women's' rights; and [C.I.D. (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049041/?ls), yet another crime thriller in which [Waheeda Rehman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0716851/?ls) made her debut.  
  
His next films, [Thirst (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050870/?ls) and [Paper Flowers (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052954/?ls), are regarded as his best work. [Thirst (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050870/?ls) was his masterpiece, about a poet trying to achieve success in a hypocritical, uncaring world. It was a box-office hit and is ranked as his greatest film ever. In contrast, [Paper Flowers (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052954/?ls) was a miserable flop at the box office: the semi-autobiographical story of a tragic love affair set against the backdrop of the film industry was deemed too morbid for the audience to swallow and went right over audience's heads. Although in later years the film received critical acclaim for its cinematography and has gained a cult following, Dutt, who had put his soul into the film, was devastated over its failure and never directed another film.  
  
Although he had sworn off directing, Dutt continued to produce and act in films, notably the period dramas [Chaudhvin Ka Chand (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053706/?ls) and [Sahib Bibi Aur Ghulam (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056436/?ls). The latter film, interestingly, is controversial because it is debated whether Dutt had ghost-directed the film. Dutt's personal life had become complicated: he had gotten romantically involved with his protégé [Waheeda Rehman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0716851/?ls) and his wife Geeta Dutt had separated from him as a result. Rehman too had distanced herself from him. Also, Dutt, an ambitious person, felt he had achieved too much too soon professionally - there was nothing better to be achieved, and this caused a vacuum in his life. Unable to cope with all the trauma and emptiness, he took to heavy drinking.  
  
On October tenth, 1964, Dutt was found dead in his bed. The cause of death was deemed a combination of alcohol and sleeping pills, although a debate still lingers over whether his death was by accident or a successful suicide attempt. Geeta Dutt suffered a nervous break-down as a result of his death and also took to alcohol, eventually drinking herself to death, dying in 1972 as a result of cirrhosis of the liver.  
  
His death was an irreplaceable loss to Indian cinema. And it was a tragic twist of fate that his films, most of which were discounted in his life-time, would be regarded as cult classics after his death. Guru Dutt would always be known, even if posthumously, as the Guru of Bollywood's Golden Age and one of the world's most important international auteurs.

Bimal Roy (July 12, 1909 - January 8, 1966) was an Indian film director. He is particularly noted for his realistic and socialistic films such as [Do Bigha Zamin (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045693/?ls), [Bandini (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056850/?ls), [Biraj Bahu (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046780/?ls), [Madhumati (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050665/?ls) which he employed to portray realism. He won a number of awards throughout his career, including eleven Filmfare Awards, two National Film Awards, and the International Prize of the Cannes Film Festival. Madhumati won 9 Filmfare Awards in 1958, a record held for 37 years.

He was one of the most acclaimed Indian film directors during 1950-60s, particularly noted for his realistic and socialistic films like Do Bigha Zamin, Parineeta, Biraj Bahu, Madhumati, Sujata, and Bandini.

 #### [5. Mehboob Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006371/?ref_=ls_t_5) 

    *   Director
    *   Producer
    *   Actor

[Mother India (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050188/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Mehboob Khan was a pioneering Indian film director and producer, best remembered for his epic film [Mother India (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050188/?ls), which won multiple Filmfare and National Awards and became India's first submission to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.  
  
Born in Bilimora, Gujarat, Khan began his journey in Bombay's film industry working in stables and eventually entered the film studios, starting as an extra and assistant during the silent era. He made his directorial debut with Al Hilal (1935) under Sagar Movietone and went on to direct significant films such as Aurat (1940), Andaz (1949), Aan (1951), Amar (1954), and Son of India (1962).  
  
In 1945, he founded his own banner, Mehboob Productions, and later established the iconic Mehboob Studios in Bandra, Mumbai in 1954. He was known for his visually grand narratives, social realism, and emotionally powerful storytelling. His work frequently tackled themes such as poverty, rural hardship, and class divide, often blending these with strong moral undertones and cinematic flair influenced by Hollywood epics. Mehboob Khan is also credited with creating the dacoit film genre and mentoring future stars including Dilip Kumar, Raj Kapoor, Sunil Dutt, Nargis, Nadira, and Rajendra Kumar.  
  
In 1961, he served on the jury of the 2nd Moscow International Film Festival and was later honored by the Indian government with the title Hidayat Kar-e-Azam. He married noted actress Sardar Akhtar in 1942. He was the President of the Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association ( IMPPA) From 1962 to 1963. He served as the president of the Film Federation of India from 1963 to 1964. His cinematic legacy endures through Mehboob Studios and the continuing influence of Mother India, which remains one of the most revered films in Indian cinema history.

Mehboob Khan produced and directed many blockbuster films, the most notable being the romantic drama Andaz (1949), the swashbuckling Aan (1951), the dramatic Amar (1954) and the social epic Mother India (1957), the latter of which was nominated for an Academy Award in 1957 and was a remake of his own 1940 film Aurat.

 #### [6. Ritwik Ghatak](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0315547/?ref_=ls_t_6) 

    *   Director

[Reason, Debate and a Story (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071707/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

Ritwik Ghatak was born on 4 November 1925 in Dacca, Bengal Presidency, British India [now in Dhaka, Bangladesh]. He was a director and writer, known for [Reason, Debate and a Story (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071707/?ls), [Musafir (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050734/?ls) and [The Cloud-Capped Star (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054073/?ls). He was married to [Surama Ghatak](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5595445/?ls). He died on 6 February 1976 in Calcutta, West Bengal, India.

Along with prominent contemporary Bengali filmmakers Satyajit Ray and Mrinal Sen, his cinema is primarily remembered for its meticulous depiction of social reality. Although their roles were often adversarial, they were ardent admirers of each other's work, and in doing so, the three directors charted the independent trajectory of parallel cinema, as a counterpoint to the mainstream fare of Hindi cinema in India.

 #### [8. Raj Kapoor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004292/?ref_=ls_t_8) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[My Name Is Joker (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066070/?ref_=ls_knf_8)

Raj Kapoor was the son of well-known Indian actor Prithviraj Kapoor, who acted both in film and on stage. After apprenticing in the Bollywood production studios of the 1940's, at 24 years of age Raj Kapoor produced, directed and acted in [Aag (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040067/?ls), with his new company, RK Films. His next production, [Barsaat (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041161/?ls), was a smash hit. In 1951, he also produced, directed and starred in [Awaara (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043306/?ls), which was another megahit, and costarred [Nargis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004291/?ls), who had appeared in Aag and Barsaat. Awaara also gained popular acclaim in Russia, where the movie and songs were dubbed into Russian. The theme song, Awaara Hoon, was popular in the East for many years. Kapoor has been dubbed "a great showman," and a filmmaker in the purest Romantic tradition, as he strove to entertain as well as address social themes close to his heart. Awaara dealt with the question of what forms an individual's moral grounding, ("nurture or nature") while incorporating comedy and stirring love scenes; in [Shree 420 (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048613/?ls) he addressed issues of poverty, unemployment and national pride in the new Indian state at the same time maintaining the audience's interest in the romantic plot. While never revolutionary in tone, many of his films explore the ability of the individual to overcome economic and environmental injustice while maintaining his/her innocence and integrity. He is quoted as believing that the individual's struggles ultimately lead to the desire for love, to care and be cared for. This is consistent with his admiration of Charles Chaplin, and Kapoor's own "tramp" (Awaara, Shree 420, [My Name Is Joker (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066070/?ls) is modeled somewhat on his mentor, though with a definite individual flair.  
  
His films demonstrate an understanding of music and direction that continue to influence Bollywood filmmaking today. Also a musician, his understanding of the musical feel of his movies gives them a storytelling fluidity equal to that of the best American movie musicals. He surrounded himself with the foremost talents in filmmaking, acting, writing (Kwaja Ahmad Abbas'), music composition ([Jaikishan Dayabhai Panchal](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1090097/?ls), 'Shankarsinh Raguwanshi'), and playback singers, including [Mukesh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006715/?ls), 'Mohamed Rafi', and [Lata Mangeshkar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0542196/?ls). Kapoor continued to make films of varying critical and popular success up until his death in 1988, and apparently considered Mera Naam Joker his personal favorite. He is still a well-known name not only in India, but in the Middle East, SE Asia, and Eastern Europe. His descendants have attempted to continue the RK Films banner.

 #### [11. Prakash Mehra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0576488/?ref_=ls_t_11) 

    *   Director
    *   Music Department
    *   Producer

[Muqaddar Ka Sikandar (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079590/?ref_=ls_knf_11)

Prakash Mehra, Born on 13th July 1939 in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh was a legendary film maker of Indian Cinema, also known as the Godfather of Amitabh Bachchan, a public and media given title, at which he often frowned upon, always clarifying that he was nobody's Godfather, fate introduced talent to talent, and history was created. Mehra started his career and life, literally from scratch, after running away from his home and village, landing up in the city of Bombay In early 1950's. As a kid, aiming for the stars, with just 13 rupees in his pocket, he began his new life, sleeping hungry on railway stations, being his first address in the city of dreams. Destiny and perseverance, guided him to the sets of Hindi cinema, where he began by observing from the sidelines, whilst doing odd jobs, starting from serving tea to the stars, then getting a chance to become a production controller, then an assistant and so on. Mehra who was never formally educated beyond grade 5, in his village school, somehow always had a knack of writing in his broken words and especially penning down his emotions, backed by years of painful experiences of an orphan child who had lost both his parents, (mother who died when he was 5, father abandoned him when he was 8) and grew up on the mean streets. As luck would have it, Mehra's creativity and hard work was not going unrecognized by his peers and seniors, who spread the positive word, finally getting him a break that turned his fortunes in 1968, when he got his directorial debut with Haseena Maan Jayegi starring Shashi Kapoor and Babita. The film which along with its music, became a huge box office money spinner, steered him on to the path of success from where there was no looking back. From here on, he went on to direct Mela (1971), which became a silver jubilee, starring Feroz and Sanjay Khan, followed by another very successful venture, Samadhi (1972), starring Dharmendra, Asha Parekh and Jaya Bhaduri. It was after the success of "Samadhi", that destiny again played a huge hand through a series of events, that lead to a phenomenal collaboration of a director and actor, the likes of which was never seen before in the history of Indian cinema, the Mehra, Bachchan collaboration. In May of 1973, with everything mortgaged, including his home and wife's jewelry, facing the very real possibility of returning to the streets, as it was also the debut of his production house "Prakash Mehra Productions", Mehra released "Zanjeer".  
  
The idea was that "Zanjeer", originally was to be made with Dharmendra as the lead star, after the success of "Samadhi". Dharmendra being the top super star at the time, opted out due to date constraints. This sent Mehra on the quest to find a replacement, and the expectations of the distributors of the time was, that a super star must be replaced by a super star, but fate would have none of it. One by one, due to some reason or the other, it just didn't workout with any of the top stars of the time. Then one fine day, Mehra received a call from the legendary actor "Pran", who Mehra not only respected as a senior and guide, but also genuinely loved and admired, fondly addressing him as "Pran sahab". Pran, asked Mehra, to check out a new kid on the block, whom he felt had talent, his name was Amitabh, also offered to accompany Mehra to a nearby theatre (Ambar Oscar) to watch his latest film, starring the great Mehmood in the lead. The two went on their way to watch the film. The wheels of fortune were set in motion, destiny through the guidance of a blessed soul "Pran", just introduced its super brilliant diamond in the rough, to its super brilliant jeweler with a keen eye. Talent was introduced to talent, Prakash Mehra was just introduced to Amitabh Bachchan.  
  
Upon the announcement of the new hero of Zanjeer, every distributor dropped the film, none would want it. Trade pundits wrote the obituary of Mehra's career, from their point of view, not only was Bachchan, not a star, but a total disaster. Not only that, there wasn't even one song in the film, where the lead hero would sing or dance, this was not only unheard of but almost incomprehensible at the time. Mehra was dubbed senile.  
  
From Mehra's point of view, there was no other star, and this is exactly how the film would be.. This also being the launch of his production house, Mehra had only 2 choices, all or nothing. It was the easiest choice he made, the jeweler knew the value of his diamond. He went all in, he released Zanjeer, with his own money on the line, in most of the major territories.  
  
The movie had an abysmal opening, empty theaters the first few days, Mehra would sit on the wall of Worli sea face in those days and contemplate, "now what"?. Bachchan suffered from a high fever, staring at oblivion himself. Then week two onwards, the phone at Mehra's small office, started ringing, it was calls from exhibitors from Calcutta, it was a phenomenon they had never seen before, there were lines longer than trains at the box office. The same story repeated in various other territories of India, cash registers at the box office went ballistic. Fortune smiled upon the little orphan kid from Bijnor. History was created, and the superstar of the millennium was born.  
  
Thereafter Prakash Mehra and Amitabh Bachchan began a journey, which resulted in 6 more, massive blockbuster hits: Hera Pheri, Khoon Pasina, Muqaddar Ka Sikandar, Laawaris, Namak Halaal and Sharaabi.  
  
Prakash Mehra was aided In creating cinema history by some of the best talent as part of his team. His blockbusters were a collaboration of super talents and legends of the time, such as music maestro duo "Kalyanji Anandji", who's music compositions are untouchable till date. Lyricists such as the great Anjaan. Mehra himself a powerhouse of writing talent, penning many of his super hit songs, such as "Apni toh jaise taise" from Laawaris, etc.. Later addition, the one and only Bappi Lahiri, who became a permanent part of Mehra's team after giving some of the best chart buster music, in Namak Halal, followed by Sharaabi. The fantastic writing duo Salim Javed were the writers of Mehra's Zanjeer. The super talented Kader Khan, wrote some of the most phenomenal dialogues of Muqaddar ka Sikandar.  
  
Apart from being work colleagues and peers, whom he greatly respected, he considered the late great Amjad Khan as one of his best friends and like family. Same was his relationship with late great Pran, legend Raj Kapoor, music maestro duo Kalyanji Anandji, and Bappi Lahiri amongst others.  
  
The final collaboration between Mehra and Bachchan was Jaadugar, which bombed at the box office and ended their untouchable successful streak, bringing an end to an era of a collaboration, the likes of which were never seen before or since.  
  
Prakash Mehra, went on to Produce and Direct "Zindagi Ek Juaa" starring Anil Kapoor and Madhuri Dixit in 1991, in 1993 produced Dalal, directed by Partho Ghosh, Starring Mithun Chakraborty in two languages, Bengali and Hindi, along with its music by Bappi Lahiri, it was a huge box office success.  
  
Mehra received a lifetime achievement award from the India Motion Picture Directors Association (IMPDA) in 2006. He also received Lifetime Achievement as Producer from IMPPA (Indian Motion Picture Producers Association) on 19 September 2008.  
  
Mr Prakash Mehra passed away on the 17th of May 2009, from complications arising out of pneumonia followed by multiple organ failure at Mumbai's Kokilaben hospital.

Although not the greatest of Indian Filmmakers, in 1973, he produced and directed Zanjeer. This mega blockbuster with Amitabh Bachchan started a relationship that spanned 7 more films, 6 being huge blockbusters (Khoon Pasina, Hera Pheri, Muqaddar ka Sikander, Laawaris, Namak Halal, Sharaabi, Jaadugar). It also launched the career of Bachchan (along with Mehra), as a top director/actor duo, spanning 2 decades of collaboration.

 #### [13. Yash Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/?ref_=ls_t_13) 

    *   Producer
    *   Director
    *   Additional Crew

[Veer Zaara (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0420332/?ref_=ls_knf_13)

Labeled the eternal romantic and with one of the best musical senses in the business, [Yash Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/?ls) is arguably India's most successful director of romantic films. Although he made action-oriented films like the ever-popular [Deewaar (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072860/?ls), it is in tackling love and its various aspects that he has been at his best. One of the few remaining commercial Indian directors who started their careers in the 1950s, he has successfully moved with the times from the socially significant [Dhool Ka Phool (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052736/?ls) to the young and cool [Dil To Pagal Hai (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118983/?ls).  
  
Yash Chopra was born in Lahore in 1932, to an accountant in the PWD division of the British Punjab administration, the youngest of eight children. He began as an assistant director to [I.S. Johar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0424102/?ls) before working with his elder brother, the legendary [B.R. Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159148/?ls); while another brother, [Dharam Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159150/?ls), worked as his cameraman. He was given his first directorial opportunity with [Dhool Ka Phool (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052736/?ls), a melodrama about illegitimacy; it became a hit and even now remains popular today. Encouraged by this success, the Chopra brothers made a few more movies together, the most notable being [Waqt (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059893/?ls), India's first multi-starrer; and [Ittefaq (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064506/?ls), a thriller. On the personal front, Chopra married [Pamela Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159158/?ls) (née Singh) in 1970, and they had two children, [Aditya Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159147/?ls) and [Uday Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159167/?ls), both working in the film industry today.  
  
In 1973, the Chopra brothers separated, with Yash Chopra founded his studio, Yash Raj Films, and launched it with [Daag: A Poem of Love (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0150251/?ls), a successful melodrama about a polygamous man. He then entered one of his best phases with two [Amitabh Bachchan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000821/?ls) classics: [Deewaar (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072860/?ls) and [Kabhi Kabhie (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074730/?ls). These movies set the standard for the 1970s and 1980s, establishing Bachchan as the greatest and most beloved Indian film star of all time. His respective roles--a bitter criminal and a sensitive, brooding poet--are considered to be his greatest performances, although complete opposites of each other.  
  
In the 1980s, Chopra went through a rough time. Two of his melodramas, [Silsila (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083081/?ls) and [Faasle (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089119/?ls); and two action-oriented films, [Mashaal (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085912/?ls) and [Vijay (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096390/?ls), flopped at the box office, although the latter became a critically acclaimed classic years later. However, he made a comeback with his musical love triangle [Chandni (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097045/?ls). The film was a huge success, with great performances by established heroine [Sridevi](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004437/?ls) and action hero [Vinod Khanna](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451396/?ls). Then came what critics and Chopra himself considered his best film, [Lamhe (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102258/?ls), a beautiful film about cross-generational love. It couldn't survive the box office, however, due to its incestuous nature.  
  
[Parampara (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107777/?ls), done for an outside producer, was a misfire, but then came the box-office hit and trend setter [Darr (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109555/?ls). Starring the then-débutant [Shah Rukh Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451321/?ls), it showed a sympathetic look at obsessive love and an emotion often overlooked in love--fear--and its success catapulted Khan to super-stardom. In 1995, Chopra turned to production and [Aditya Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159147/?ls) made his directorial debut with [Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112870/?ls), which had the longest-running initial release in cinema history. He directed one more film, [Dil To Pagal Hai (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118983/?ls), a love story set against the theater, which became a huge success and a cult hit, before he retired from directing. However, in 2004, he made a grand comeback with [Veer Zaara (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0420332/?ls), a touching cross-border love story, which he said would be his last directorial effort.  
  
The ages of the director and playback singer [Lata Mangeshkar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0542196/?ls), his muse, proved you need to be young, as well as crazy, at heart, to be a true romantic....

Some of his last movies like Veer-Zara don't match his reputation, but his earlier movies are one of the best for ex. Darr, Lamhe, Mashaal etc.

 #### [20. Mani Ratnam](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0711745/?ref_=ls_t_20) 

    *   Writer
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Guru (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0499375/?ref_=ls_knf_20)

The man who revolutionized Tamil-language cinema, Mani Ratnam is the biggest director in south India and one of the most respected directors in all of India. Each of his films contain its own unique style, with beautifully photographed songs and unique back-lighting. However, his films contain substance as well as style--Ratnam has dealt with a wide variety of topics, from the classic Indian love story to political thrillers.  
  
He was born in Madras in 1956. Filmmaking was in his blood; he was the son of film producer 'Venus Gopalratnam' and his brother was [G. Venkateswaran](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1234765/?ls), a film distributor turned producer. Ironically, however, he studied at Madras University and received a management degree at the Jamnalal Bajaj Institute of Management Studies in Mumbai, and had initially started out as a management consultant. His first film, [Pallavi Anu Pallavi (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086075/?ls), starring [Anil Kapoor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0438463/?ls), didn't make many waves, although it won the State Award from Karnataka that year, but even though he made two films in Tamil and one in Malayalam, nothing worked for him until he broke through with [Mouna Ragam (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091559/?ls). Starring [Revathi](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0720763/?ls), the film told the tale of a woman who, although forced into an arranged marriage, chooses to maintain a platonic relationship with her husband. The film was noted for its sophisticated approach and execution of an extremely sensitive topic.  
  
His next film, [Nayakan (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093603/?ls), was also arguably his greatest. A take-off on [Francis Ford Coppola](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000338/?ls)' legendary [The Godfather (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068646/?ls), it established Ratnam as the leading director of Tamil-language Cinema and won its leading actor [Kamal Haasan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0352032/?ls) the National Award for Best Actor. The film draws on 30 years of Tamil Nadu's celebrity images and directly played to the anti-Hindi feelings of Tamil Nadu when the protagonist, beaten up, tells the Hindi policeman in Bombay, "If I ever hit you, you will die!"  
  
Then came the best of his early work - [Agni Natchathiram (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094621/?ls), [Geethanjali (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097437/?ls), and [Anjali (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099043/?ls). The first was a tale of conflict between two step-brothers. Shot with glossy camera work, the film resembled a cross between an advertisement and a music video, and set a trend for a whole new visual style in Tamil-language Cinema. The next, [Geethanjali (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097437/?ls), shot in Ooty to create a soft and poetic mood, was a touching love story between two terminally ill people with less than six months left. The third, [Anjali (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099043/?ls), about a disabled child brought back to her family with two normal children had been chosen by India to be sent to the Oscars for Best Foreign-language Film, but it did not receive a nomination. The next year saw his first, and only collaboration so far, with the Tamil superstar Rajni Kant in the film [Thalapathi (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101649/?ls). It also starred Mamooty, along side a host of other actor. This star studded film was a gritty tale of an orphan who grows up to become a notorious gang member in Chennai. The story was inspired by the great epic of Mahabharata.  
  
It was [Roja (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105271/?ls) that made Ratnam a household name all over India. A patriotic love story set against the backdrop of Kashmiri terrorism, the film was dubbed in Hindi and became a huge national success. It enforced Ratnam as a director of style and substance, as well as proving a highly auspicious debut for the now-acclaimed music director [A.R. Rahman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006246/?ls), whom Ratnam had discovered. It helped that India's at-the-time election commissioner T. N. Seshan took the rare step of officially endorsing the film. [Thiruda Thiruda (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108329/?ls), a remake of [Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064115/?ls) was a misfire, but Ratnam bounced back with [Bombay (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112553/?ls), a politically charged romance between a Hindu man and a Muslim woman during the 1993 riots in Mumbai. The film underwent some controversy due to its slightly anti-Muslim viewpoint, but it contributed widely to the success of the film.  
  
Continuing his political obsession, Ratnam made [Iruvar (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119385/?ls), based on the MGR-Karunanidhi affair, and [Dil Se.. (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0164538/?ls), which starred superstars [Manisha Koirala](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0463539/?ls) and [Shah Rukh Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451321/?ls). The latter was Ratnam's first Hindi-language film. Based on the northeast Indian problem, it told the story of a radio executive and a revolutionary. It had an excellent cast, beautifully crafted scenes, and most of all one of [A.R. Rahman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006246/?ls)'s greatest tunes--but did not go down too well with the audience, who hailed it as a strange and confusing film that headed nowhere. However, today it is held as ahead of its time, being that it was shot pre-9/11, and is now hailed as a contemporary classic.  
  
He returned to familiar ground with [Alai Payuthey (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0242256/?ls), which tackled the story of a couple in love that goes through the trials and tribulations of marriage. His subsequent film, [Kannathil Muthamittal (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0312859/?ls), which told the tale of an adopted girl meeting her terrorist mother, saw Ratnam back in form as one of the greatest storytellers in Indian Cinema. His next film, [Yuva (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0382383/?ls), saw Ratnam return to Hindi-language cinema after six years, but in spite of some fine flourishes, the film largely failed to work. However, don't take him too lightly: he is sure to return with something new next time....

An accomplished and award-winning producer-director-writer-actor-singer, Farhan Akhtar is the ultimate Bollywood multi-hyphenate. Born in 1974 to prolific Indian film writer and poet, [Javed Akhtar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0015287/?ls) and writer-director, [Honey Irani](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0409790/?ls) , Farhan was raised in an environment where creativity and originality of thought were encouraged. This has made him a maverick whose films reflect refreshingly new content that easily strikes a chord with filmgoers.  
  
In 1999, Farhan collaborated with [Ritesh Sidhwani](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1032700/?ls), a friend who shared his passion for good cinema, to form Excel Entertainment, a production banner that has become synonymous with excellence in film-making.  
  
Debuting at the age of 26, as a writer, director, and producer with [Dil Chahta Hai (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0292490/?ls) a coming-of-age film that has gained cult status, Farhan came to be lauded for his honest, path-breaking writing and his ability to extract mature performances from his cast. The film won Farhan his first National Award for 'Best Hindi Feature Film' along with Filmfare awards for 'Best Feature Film - Critics Choice' and 'Best Screenplay'.  
  
Almost two decades later, this film continues to influence a generation of filmmakers.  
  
Seven years after his dream debut as a writer-director, Farhan debuted as an actor-singer in [Rock On!! (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1230165/?ls) Yet another runaway success, the film secured him a second National Award for 'Best Hindi Feature Film' and a Filmfare award for 'Best Debut Performance'.  
  
The dream run continued with [Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1562872/?ls) which released in 2011 to much popular and critical acclaim, winning him three Filmfare awards for 'Best Film', 'Best Actor in a supporting role' and 'Best Dialogue'.  
  
His next, a biopic on Indian athlete [Milkha Singh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2245260/?ls), popularly known as 'the Flying Sikh', was entitled [Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2356180/?ls).  
  
He essayed the role with such integrity that it set the standard for other actors considering to play titular protagonists in biopics. Deservingly, Farhan swept all awards that year for 'Best Actor' as did the film for 'Best Film'. It also claimed the National award for 'Best Popular Film providing Wholesome Entertainment.'  
  
His most recent release [The Sky Is Pink (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8902990/?ls) premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and received a 15-minute standing ovation from the audience at the Roy Thomson Hall.  
  
In addition to his contribution to Indian cinema, Farhan has initiated and supported a plethora of social causes. In 2012, he founded MARD (Men against Rape & Discrimination), an initiative that raises awareness about gender-related issues amongst the youth of India. Recognizing his sustained efforts, Farhan was made the first male UNwomen goodwill ambassador (South Asia) in 2014.  
  
Additionally, Farhan feeds his passion for music by writing, composing and performing live with his band FarhanLive.  
  
His English language debut album 'Echoes' released in March 2019 to critical acclaim.  
  
He has 2 daughters and lives in Mumbai, India.

[Bhuvan Shome (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064086/?ref_=ls_knf_24)

Sen is one of his nation's most politically active filmakers. After having studied physics at university in Calcutta, Sen worked as a freelance journalist, a salesman of patent medicines and a sound technician in a film studio. In the mid-1940s he joined the Indian People's Theatre Association and at that time began to read about and study film. The association had links to the Communist Party of India and this heralded the beginning of Sen's involvement with Marxist politics. In 1956 Sen made his debut with [Raat Bhore (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049649/?ls), the first of his 30 (as of 2002) films. Although his first film was openly political, he achieved national status as the director of a comedy, [Bhuvan Shome (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064086/?ls). Influenced by Italian neorealism and the work of fellow countryman [Satyajit Ray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006249/?ls), Sen used location shooting and non-professional casts in his early films. By the 1970s he was making wider use of symbolism and allegory. Although he remains politically committed, Sen feels that the "difference between party Marxists and a private Marxist like me is that others think they pocketed truth, whereas I am always in search of truth... " Sen's films have won numerous international awards. [The Case Is Closed (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084198/?ls), a scathing look at the hypocritical reaction of a bourgeois Calcutta family to the death of a servant boy, took home the Jury Prize from the 1983 Cannes Film Festival.

**Shekhar Kulbhushan Kapur** (born 6 December 1945) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people") filmmaker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1) Born into the [Anand-Sahni family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand-Sahni_family "Anand-Sahni family"), Kapur is the recipient of several accolades, including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), a [National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award"), a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review") and three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), in addition to nomination for a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award").

Kapur became known in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with his recurring role in the television series _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(TV\_series) "Khandaan (TV series)")_. He then made his directorial debut with [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")_[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ in 1983, before gaining widespread acclaim with _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ in 1987. He then gained international recognition and acclaim in 1994 with [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, based on the infamous [Indian bandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacoity "Dacoity") and politician [Phoolan Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoolan_Devi "Phoolan Devi"). The film premiered in the directors' fortnight section of the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival") and was screened at the [Edinburgh Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Festival_Fringe "Edinburgh Festival Fringe").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)

Kapur achieved further international prominence with the 1998 period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictionalized account of the reign of [English Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England"), which was nominated for seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He then directed [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")_[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_ (2002). In 2007, he directed _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, the sequel to his 1998 film.

Shekhar Kapur was awarded the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Balakrishna,_Ajith,_Shekhar_Kapur,_Shobana_honoured_with_Padma_Bhushan,_Arijit_Singh,_Ricky_Kej_conferred_with_Padma_Shri-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Shekhar was born on 6 December 1945 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_(British_India) "Punjab (British India)"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India "British India"), in a [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family to Kulbhushan Kapoor, a doctor with a flourishing practice, and his wife Sheel Kanta Kapoor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1)

Whilst travelling on a train from the newly created Pakistan to India, a massacre took place; Kapur's mother Sheel played dead and hid both him and his sister under her body.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5) Reflecting on this, Kapur stated that the [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") happened through "the blood of one people".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5)

The nephew of famous Indian actor [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") (Kapur's mother Sheel Kanta was the sister of actors [Chetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), Dev and [Vijay Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay_Anand_(Hindi_film_maker) "Vijay Anand (Hindi film maker)")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-6)), he was discouraged from getting into films by his father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-NYT-7) Kapur is the only son of his parents and he has three sisters. One of his sisters, Neelu, was the first wife of actor [Navin Nischol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navin_Nischol "Navin Nischol"), while another sister, Aruna, is the wife of actor [Parikshit Sahni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parikshit_Sahni "Parikshit Sahni"). His third and youngest sister is [Sohaila Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sohaila_Kapur "Sohaila Kapur").

Kapur attended [Modern School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_School_(New_Delhi) "Modern School (New Delhi)") of [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-8) He studied economics at [St. Stephen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_College,_Delhi "St. Stephen's College, Delhi"). At 22, he became a [Chartered Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_Accountant "Chartered Accountant") with the [ICAEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Chartered_Accountants_in_England_and_Wales "Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales") in England, having studied accountancy at the behest of his parents.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-10) He then started his career working with a multinational oil company. He moved to the United Kingdom in 1970, and spent several years working as an accountant and [management consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management_consultant "Management consultant").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-11)

## Filmmaking career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Filmmaking career")]

### In India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: In India")]

He turned director with the family drama _[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ (1983), starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi") and a young [Jugal Hansraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jugal_Hansraj "Jugal Hansraj") and [Urmila Matondkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar "Urmila Matondkar"). The plot followed the story of an illegitimate boy who struggles to find acceptance from his stepmother. He then directed the 1987 science-fiction film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_, starring [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Amrish Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrish_Puri "Amrish Puri") in his most famous role as the villain Mogambo. Puri's most famous dialogue in this film "Mogambo Khush Hua" is still remembered.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-12) In 1994 he directed the critically acclaimed _Bandit Queen_[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-13) and played a cameo in the film as a truck driver.

Kapur was infamous for abandoning several films in which he was originally the director.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-14) He was originally the director of the 1989 film _[Joshilaay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshilaay "Joshilaay")_, which starred [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Meenakshi Sheshadri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Sheshadri "Meenakshi Sheshadri") before leaving the production halfway, and its producer Sibti Hassan Rizvi stepped in to complete the film. In 1992, he had shot some scenes for _[Barsaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barsaat\_(1995\_film) "Barsaat (1995 film)")_, which was originally titled _Champion_[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-15) and was going to be the debut film of [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), but he left the production and was replaced by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). In 1995, he partly directed _[Dushmani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushmani:\_A\_Violent\_Love\_Story "Dushmani: A Violent Love Story")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala") before its producer Bunty Soorma stepped in to complete the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-16)

Kapur was the executive producer of the film _[The Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guru\_(2002\_film) "The Guru (2002 film)")_. He established an Indian film company with [Ram Gopal Verma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Gopal_Verma "Ram Gopal Verma") and Mani Ratnam, though the group has thus far produced only one film, _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), starring [Shahrukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala"). Kapur executive-produced the [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood")-themed [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre")_[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ by [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber"), which ran in London's [the West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in New York City for 1 year.

In 2016, Kapur delivers an autobiographical film and documentary about [Amma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi "Mata Amritanandamayi"), well known as [Mata Amritanandamayi Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi_Devi "Mata Amritanandamayi Devi"), called "The Science of Compassion".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-17)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International")]

In 1998, he received international recognition for the second time after _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, when he directed the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictional account of the reign of [British Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England") nominated for seven [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). The 2007 sequel, _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, was nominated for two [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He was accused of being anti-British by [British tabloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_tabloid "British tabloid") for his inaccurate portrayal of the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") in the 2002 movie _[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_. He denied the accusations and stated that he was merely "anti-colonisation".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-18)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

Kapur started his career as an actor in the movie _[Jaan Hazir Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan\_Hazir\_Hai "Jaan Hazir Hai")_ (1975)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-19) starring [Prem Kishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Kishen "Prem Kishen") and [Trilok Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilok_Kapoor "Trilok Kapoor") and later in _[Toote Khilone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toote\_Khilone "Toote Khilone")_, in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood"). He appeared in several Hindi television dramas, such as _[Udaan (Doordarshan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udaan\_(1989\_TV\_series) "Udaan (1989 TV series)")_, opposite [Kavita Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavita_Chaudhary "Kavita Chaudhary"), _Upanyaas_[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-20) (Doordarshan) opposite Nisha Singh, and _Masoom_ opposite Neena Gupta.

He served as judge on the reality TV series _[India's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Got\_Talent "India's Got Talent")_, aired on [Colors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colors_TV "Colors TV").

In an unusual role for him, Kapur provided the voice of [Mohandas Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohandas_Gandhi "Mohandas Gandhi") in the [Charkha Audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charkha_Audiobooks "Charkha Audiobooks") title of _[The Story of My Experiments with Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Story\_of\_My\_Experiments\_with\_Truth "The Story of My Experiments with Truth")_, alongside [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das") as narrator.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2013, Kapur hosted the TV show _[Pradhanmantri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradhanmantri\_(TV\_Series) "Pradhanmantri (TV Series)")_ on [ABP News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABP_News "ABP News"). On the show, which aims to bring never-seen-before facets of Indian history, he was the narrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-21)

### Comic book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Comic book publishing")]

Further information: [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics")

In 2006, Kapur formed [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics") and Virgin Animation, an entertainment company focused on creating new stories and characters for a global audience. The [Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Comics#Shakti "Virgin Comics") titles of Kapur and [Deepak Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chopra "Deepak Chopra")'s company debuted with _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(comics) "Devi (comics)")_ and _[The Sadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sadhu "The Sadhu")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)_Devi_ is about "a fierce feminine warrior, stronger than the Gods themselves ... a champion of the heavens, and the protector of man", while _The Sadhu_ "is about one man's choice between his spiritual oath and his human instinct."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kapur had a relationship for seven years with actress [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-23) He first was married to Medha Gujral, niece of former Indian Prime Minister [Inder Kumar Gujral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inder_Kumar_Gujral "Inder Kumar Gujral").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-24) They divorced in 1994.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-25) She died on 25 November 2014 at a hospital in New York City of liver failure following a second heart and first kidney transplant.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-26) Kapur later married actress [Suchitra Krishnamoorthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suchitra_Krishnamoorthi "Suchitra Krishnamoorthi") in 1999.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-27) They have a daughter named Kaveri Kapur.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-28) The couple divorced in 2007.

In March 2020, Krishnamoorthi filed a case against Kapur over a property dispute concerning their daughter Kaveri.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-29) She claimed that the property rightfully belongs to their daughter, but has been rented to actor [Kabir Bedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir_Bedi "Kabir Bedi") and his wife Parveen.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-30)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

In 2000, he received [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), the fourth highest civilian award in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Padma_Awards-31) In 2010, he served as one of the Jury Members in international competition at the [63rd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Cannes_Film_Festival "2010 Cannes Film Festival").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-32) In 2020, Kapur became the president of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-33)

In 2023, Kapur served as the chairperson of the International competition Jury at the [54th International Film Festival of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_of_India "54th International Film Festival of India") held from 20 November to 28 November.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-34)
