**Shekhar Kulbhushan Kapur** (born 6 December 1945) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people") filmmaker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1) Born into the [Anand-Sahni family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand-Sahni_family "Anand-Sahni family"), Kapur is the recipient of several accolades, including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), a [National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award"), a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review") and three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), in addition to nomination for a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award").

Kapur became known in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with his recurring role in the television series _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(TV\_series) "Khandaan (TV series)")_. He then made his directorial debut with [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")_[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ in 1983, before gaining widespread acclaim with _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ in 1987. He then gained international recognition and acclaim in 1994 with [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, based on the infamous [Indian bandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacoity "Dacoity") and politician [Phoolan Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoolan_Devi "Phoolan Devi"). The film premiered in the directors' fortnight section of the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival") and was screened at the [Edinburgh Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Festival_Fringe "Edinburgh Festival Fringe").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)

Kapur achieved further international prominence with the 1998 period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictionalized account of the reign of [English Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England"), which was nominated for seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He then directed [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")_[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_ (2002). In 2007, he directed _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, the sequel to his 1998 film.

Shekhar Kapur was awarded the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Balakrishna,_Ajith,_Shekhar_Kapur,_Shobana_honoured_with_Padma_Bhushan,_Arijit_Singh,_Ricky_Kej_conferred_with_Padma_Shri-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Shekhar was born on 6 December 1945 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_(British_India) "Punjab (British India)"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India "British India"), in a [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family to Kulbhushan Kapoor, a doctor with a flourishing practice, and his wife Sheel Kanta Kapoor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1)

Whilst travelling on a train from the newly created Pakistan to India, a massacre took place; Kapur's mother Sheel played dead and hid both him and his sister under her body.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5) Reflecting on this, Kapur stated that the [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") happened through "the blood of one people".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5)

The nephew of famous Indian actor [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") (Kapur's mother Sheel Kanta was the sister of actors [Chetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), Dev and [Vijay Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay_Anand_(Hindi_film_maker) "Vijay Anand (Hindi film maker)")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-6)), he was discouraged from getting into films by his father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-NYT-7) Kapur is the only son of his parents and he has three sisters. One of his sisters, Neelu, was the first wife of actor [Navin Nischol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navin_Nischol "Navin Nischol"), while another sister, Aruna, is the wife of actor [Parikshit Sahni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parikshit_Sahni "Parikshit Sahni"). His third and youngest sister is [Sohaila Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sohaila_Kapur "Sohaila Kapur").

Kapur attended [Modern School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_School_(New_Delhi) "Modern School (New Delhi)") of [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-8) He studied economics at [St. Stephen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_College,_Delhi "St. Stephen's College, Delhi"). At 22, he became a [Chartered Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_Accountant "Chartered Accountant") with the [ICAEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Chartered_Accountants_in_England_and_Wales "Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales") in England, having studied accountancy at the behest of his parents.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-10) He then started his career working with a multinational oil company. He moved to the United Kingdom in 1970, and spent several years working as an accountant and [management consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management_consultant "Management consultant").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-11)

## Filmmaking career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Filmmaking career")]

### In India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: In India")]

He turned director with the family drama _[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ (1983), starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi") and a young [Jugal Hansraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jugal_Hansraj "Jugal Hansraj") and [Urmila Matondkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar "Urmila Matondkar"). The plot followed the story of an illegitimate boy who struggles to find acceptance from his stepmother. He then directed the 1987 science-fiction film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_, starring [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Amrish Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrish_Puri "Amrish Puri") in his most famous role as the villain Mogambo. Puri's most famous dialogue in this film "Mogambo Khush Hua" is still remembered.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-12) In 1994 he directed the critically acclaimed _Bandit Queen_[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-13) and played a cameo in the film as a truck driver.

Kapur was infamous for abandoning several films in which he was originally the director.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-14) He was originally the director of the 1989 film _[Joshilaay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshilaay "Joshilaay")_, which starred [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Meenakshi Sheshadri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Sheshadri "Meenakshi Sheshadri") before leaving the production halfway, and its producer Sibti Hassan Rizvi stepped in to complete the film. In 1992, he had shot some scenes for _[Barsaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barsaat\_(1995\_film) "Barsaat (1995 film)")_, which was originally titled _Champion_[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-15) and was going to be the debut film of [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), but he left the production and was replaced by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). In 1995, he partly directed _[Dushmani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushmani:\_A\_Violent\_Love\_Story "Dushmani: A Violent Love Story")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala") before its producer Bunty Soorma stepped in to complete the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-16)

Kapur was the executive producer of the film _[The Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guru\_(2002\_film) "The Guru (2002 film)")_. He established an Indian film company with [Ram Gopal Verma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Gopal_Verma "Ram Gopal Verma") and Mani Ratnam, though the group has thus far produced only one film, _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), starring [Shahrukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala"). Kapur executive-produced the [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood")-themed [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre")_[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ by [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber"), which ran in London's [the West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in New York City for 1 year.

In 2016, Kapur delivers an autobiographical film and documentary about [Amma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi "Mata Amritanandamayi"), well known as [Mata Amritanandamayi Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi_Devi "Mata Amritanandamayi Devi"), called "The Science of Compassion".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-17)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International")]

In 1998, he received international recognition for the second time after _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, when he directed the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictional account of the reign of [British Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England") nominated for seven [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). The 2007 sequel, _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, was nominated for two [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He was accused of being anti-British by [British tabloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_tabloid "British tabloid") for his inaccurate portrayal of the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") in the 2002 movie _[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_. He denied the accusations and stated that he was merely "anti-colonisation".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-18)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

Kapur started his career as an actor in the movie _[Jaan Hazir Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan\_Hazir\_Hai "Jaan Hazir Hai")_ (1975)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-19) starring [Prem Kishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Kishen "Prem Kishen") and [Trilok Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilok_Kapoor "Trilok Kapoor") and later in _[Toote Khilone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toote\_Khilone "Toote Khilone")_, in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood"). He appeared in several Hindi television dramas, such as _[Udaan (Doordarshan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udaan\_(1989\_TV\_series) "Udaan (1989 TV series)")_, opposite [Kavita Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavita_Chaudhary "Kavita Chaudhary"), _Upanyaas_[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-20) (Doordarshan) opposite Nisha Singh, and _Masoom_ opposite Neena Gupta.

He served as judge on the reality TV series _[India's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Got\_Talent "India's Got Talent")_, aired on [Colors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colors_TV "Colors TV").

In an unusual role for him, Kapur provided the voice of [Mohandas Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohandas_Gandhi "Mohandas Gandhi") in the [Charkha Audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charkha_Audiobooks "Charkha Audiobooks") title of _[The Story of My Experiments with Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Story\_of\_My\_Experiments\_with\_Truth "The Story of My Experiments with Truth")_, alongside [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das") as narrator.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2013, Kapur hosted the TV show _[Pradhanmantri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradhanmantri\_(TV\_Series) "Pradhanmantri (TV Series)")_ on [ABP News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABP_News "ABP News"). On the show, which aims to bring never-seen-before facets of Indian history, he was the narrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-21)

### Comic book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Comic book publishing")]

Further information: [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics")

In 2006, Kapur formed [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics") and Virgin Animation, an entertainment company focused on creating new stories and characters for a global audience. The [Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Comics#Shakti "Virgin Comics") titles of Kapur and [Deepak Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chopra "Deepak Chopra")'s company debuted with _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(comics) "Devi (comics)")_ and _[The Sadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sadhu "The Sadhu")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)_Devi_ is about "a fierce feminine warrior, stronger than the Gods themselves ... a champion of the heavens, and the protector of man", while _The Sadhu_ "is about one man's choice between his spiritual oath and his human instinct."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kapur had a relationship for seven years with actress [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-23) He first was married to Medha Gujral, niece of former Indian Prime Minister [Inder Kumar Gujral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inder_Kumar_Gujral "Inder Kumar Gujral").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-24) They divorced in 1994.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-25) She died on 25 November 2014 at a hospital in New York City of liver failure following a second heart and first kidney transplant.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-26) Kapur later married actress [Suchitra Krishnamoorthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suchitra_Krishnamoorthi "Suchitra Krishnamoorthi") in 1999.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-27) They have a daughter named Kaveri Kapur.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-28) The couple divorced in 2007.

In March 2020, Krishnamoorthi filed a case against Kapur over a property dispute concerning their daughter Kaveri.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-29) She claimed that the property rightfully belongs to their daughter, but has been rented to actor [Kabir Bedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir_Bedi "Kabir Bedi") and his wife Parveen.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-30)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

In 2000, he received [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), the fourth highest civilian award in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Padma_Awards-31) In 2010, he served as one of the Jury Members in international competition at the [63rd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Cannes_Film_Festival "2010 Cannes Film Festival").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-32) In 2020, Kapur became the president of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-33)

In 2023, Kapur served as the chairperson of the International competition Jury at the [54th International Film Festival of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_of_India "54th International Film Festival of India") held from 20 November to 28 November.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-34)

**Michael James Radford** (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)") of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") and [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") (in his final role), the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") adaptation _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_, the [true crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_crime "True crime") drama _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, for which he won the [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards") for [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction") and [Best Film Not in the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language"), and earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay").

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Radford was born on 24 February 1946, in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_and_provinces_of_British_India "Presidencies and provinces of British India"), to a British father and an Austrian [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") mother. He was educated at [Bedford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_School "Bedford School") before attending [Worcester College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_College,_Oxford "Worcester College, Oxford"). After teaching for a few years, he went to the [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School"), becoming a student there in its inaugural year.

Between 1976 and 1982, Radford worked as a documentary film maker, mostly on projects for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), covering subjects such as Scottish islanders on the [Isle of Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Lewis "Isle of Lewis") in the [Outer Hebrides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Hebrides "Outer Hebrides") who believe in the literal truth of the Bible: _The Last Stronghold of the Pure Gospel_; the soprano [Isobel Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isobel_Buchanan "Isobel Buchanan"): _La Belle Isobel_; the singer songwriter [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"): _[Van Morrison in Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van\_Morrison\_in\_Ireland "Van Morrison in Ireland")_; and the self-explanatory _The Making of [The Pirates of Penzance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pirates\_of\_Penzance "The Pirates of Penzance")_. On the last two of these, Radford worked with the [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer")[Roger Deakins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Deakins "Roger Deakins"), who would later shoot two of Radford's feature films; _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_ and _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_. Another notable early work was _[Another Time, Another Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another\_Time,\_Another\_Place\_(1983\_film) "Another Time, Another Place (1983 film)")_ (1983), a feature film set in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and centred on a love story between a local woman and an [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[POW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Radford came to international attention with _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_, his adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_, starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") as Winston Smith, and in which [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") gave his final film performance.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) The film was made in the time and place ([London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), April–June 1984) at which the book was set.

Radford's next film, released in 1987, was _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, a period drama set in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") during the 1940s.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) Radford again wrote the screenplay, an adaptation of the novel by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)") also called _White Mischief_.

Michael Radford is most widely known as the writer and director of the 1994 film _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, which Radford adapted from the novel _[Ardiente Paciencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardiente\_paciencia "Ardiente paciencia")_ by [Antonio Skármeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Sk%C3%A1rmeta "Antonio Skármeta").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) The massive international success of the film (for many years it was the largest grossing non-English language film ever made) led to international acclaim for Radford and the star of the film [Massimo Troisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Troisi "Massimo Troisi"). Tragically, Troisi died, aged 41, the day after the filming of _Il Postino_ was completed. The film won many international film awards including the 'Best Film Not in the English Language' [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts "British Academy of Film and Television Arts") for Radford, who was also nominated for the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay")[Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards").

In 2000, Radford's film _[Dancing at the Blue Iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing\_at\_the\_Blue\_Iguana "Dancing at the Blue Iguana")_ was released.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In a departure from his more usual development technique, namely adapting novels, this film was largely improvised, although Radford shared the screenwriting credit with [David Linter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Linter?action=edit&redlink=1 "David Linter (page does not exist)").

In 2004, Radford directed _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_ (2004).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) He adapted the [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") play (see: [Shakespearean comedies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespearean_comedies "Shakespearean comedies")), and the film stars [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as [Shylock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shylock "Shylock") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons") as [Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_(Merchant_of_Venice) "Antonio (Merchant of Venice)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In 2007, he reunited [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore") and [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine") (who had already been together in 1984 for _[Blame it on Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blame\_it\_on\_Rio "Blame it on Rio")_) in _[Flawless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flawless\_(2007\_film) "Flawless (2007 film)")_, a diamond heist story set in 1960.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) His most recent film is _[Elsa & Fred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa\_&\_Fred\_(2014\_film) "Elsa & Fred (2014 film)")_ (2014), a romantic comedy starring [Shirley MacLaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_MacLaine "Shirley MacLaine") and [Christopher Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Plummer "Christopher Plummer").

Radford directed his first play in 2000, a [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") production of _[The Seven Year Itch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seven\_Year\_Itch "The Seven Year Itch")_. This was an adaptation of [Billy Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Wilder "Billy Wilder")'s 1955 film starring [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Radford has a son, Felix (born 1991), from his first marriage to Iseult Teran. He also has a daughter, Amaryllis (born 2005), and a son, Linus (born 2010), with his current wife, Emma Tweed.

In addition to English (his first language), he speaks fluent Spanish, French, Italian, and some Mandarin.

In September 2013, he took part in the Clipper Round the World Sailing Race, in which he raced one of 12 identical 70-foot racing yachts from London to Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-3)

**Michael James Radford** (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)") of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") and [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") (in his final role), the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") adaptation _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_, the [true crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_crime "True crime") drama _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, for which he won the [BAFTA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Awards "BAFTA Awards") for [Best Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Direction "BAFTA Award for Best Direction") and [Best Film Not in the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language"), and earned [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations for [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay").

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Radford was born on 24 February 1946, in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_and_provinces_of_British_India "Presidencies and provinces of British India"), to a British father and an Austrian [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") mother. He was educated at [Bedford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_School "Bedford School") before attending [Worcester College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_College,_Oxford "Worcester College, Oxford"). After teaching for a few years, he went to the [National Film and Television School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_and_Television_School "National Film and Television School"), becoming a student there in its inaugural year.

Between 1976 and 1982, Radford worked as a documentary film maker, mostly on projects for the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), covering subjects such as Scottish islanders on the [Isle of Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isle_of_Lewis "Isle of Lewis") in the [Outer Hebrides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Hebrides "Outer Hebrides") who believe in the literal truth of the Bible: _The Last Stronghold of the Pure Gospel_; the soprano [Isobel Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isobel_Buchanan "Isobel Buchanan"): _La Belle Isobel_; the singer songwriter [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison"): _[Van Morrison in Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van\_Morrison\_in\_Ireland "Van Morrison in Ireland")_; and the self-explanatory _The Making of [The Pirates of Penzance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pirates\_of\_Penzance "The Pirates of Penzance")_. On the last two of these, Radford worked with the [cinematographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinematographer "Cinematographer")[Roger Deakins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Deakins "Roger Deakins"), who would later shoot two of Radford's feature films; _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_ and _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_. Another notable early work was _[Another Time, Another Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another\_Time,\_Another\_Place\_(1983\_film) "Another Time, Another Place (1983 film)")_ (1983), a feature film set in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and centred on a love story between a local woman and an [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[POW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Radford came to international attention with _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four\_(1984\_film) "Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984 film)")_, his adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_, starring [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt") as Winston Smith, and in which [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") gave his final film performance.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) The film was made in the time and place ([London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), April–June 1984) at which the book was set.

Radford's next film, released in 1987, was _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, a period drama set in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") during the 1940s.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) Radford again wrote the screenplay, an adaptation of the novel by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)") also called _White Mischief_.

Michael Radford is most widely known as the writer and director of the 1994 film _[Il Postino: The Postman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il\_Postino:\_The\_Postman "Il Postino: The Postman")_, which Radford adapted from the novel _[Ardiente Paciencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardiente\_paciencia "Ardiente paciencia")_ by [Antonio Skármeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Sk%C3%A1rmeta "Antonio Skármeta").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) The massive international success of the film (for many years it was the largest grossing non-English language film ever made) led to international acclaim for Radford and the star of the film [Massimo Troisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Troisi "Massimo Troisi"). Tragically, Troisi died, aged 41, the day after the filming of _Il Postino_ was completed. The film won many international film awards including the 'Best Film Not in the English Language' [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_of_Film_and_Television_Arts "British Academy of Film and Television Arts") for Radford, who was also nominated for the [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") and [Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Writing_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Writing Adapted Screenplay")[Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards").

In 2000, Radford's film _[Dancing at the Blue Iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing\_at\_the\_Blue\_Iguana "Dancing at the Blue Iguana")_ was released.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In a departure from his more usual development technique, namely adapting novels, this film was largely improvised, although Radford shared the screenwriting credit with [David Linter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Linter?action=edit&redlink=1 "David Linter (page does not exist)").

In 2004, Radford directed _[The Merchant of Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Merchant\_of\_Venice\_(2004\_film) "The Merchant of Venice (2004 film)")_ (2004).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) He adapted the [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") play (see: [Shakespearean comedies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespearean_comedies "Shakespearean comedies")), and the film stars [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as [Shylock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shylock "Shylock") and [Jeremy Irons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Irons "Jeremy Irons") as [Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_(Merchant_of_Venice) "Antonio (Merchant of Venice)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) In 2007, he reunited [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore") and [Michael Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Caine "Michael Caine") (who had already been together in 1984 for _[Blame it on Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blame\_it\_on\_Rio "Blame it on Rio")_) in _[Flawless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flawless\_(2007\_film) "Flawless (2007 film)")_, a diamond heist story set in 1960.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT2-2) His most recent film is _[Elsa & Fred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa\_&\_Fred\_(2014\_film) "Elsa & Fred (2014 film)")_ (2014), a romantic comedy starring [Shirley MacLaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirley_MacLaine "Shirley MacLaine") and [Christopher Plummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Plummer "Christopher Plummer").

Radford directed his first play in 2000, a [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") production of _[The Seven Year Itch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Seven\_Year\_Itch "The Seven Year Itch")_. This was an adaptation of [Billy Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Wilder "Billy Wilder")'s 1955 film starring [Marilyn Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Monroe "Marilyn Monroe").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Radford has a son, Felix (born 1991), from his first marriage to Iseult Teran. He also has a daughter, Amaryllis (born 2005), and a son, Linus (born 2010), with his current wife, Emma Tweed.

In addition to English (his first language), he speaks fluent Spanish, French, Italian, and some Mandarin.

In September 2013, he took part in the Clipper Round the World Sailing Race, in which he raced one of 12 identical 70-foot racing yachts from London to Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-3)
